clue.text: Yo-yo game ceases to worry; win or lose, I don't mind

definitions.text: win or lose, I don't mind

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug and shake it about, as a dog worries a bone, so these letters get jumbled

explanation.surface: A child's toy game stops being a cause of anxiety, and the speaker shrugs off whether they win or lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yo-yo' sits nicely with the indifferent shrug that follows, but it is just letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a casual attitude to gain and loss: whatever arrives easily can depart just as easily, so the speaker doesn't care.

clue.text: Embarrassingly ghastly French kid?

parts.note: the French phrase literally means a terrible child, one whose candour embarrasses the grown-ups around them

explanation.surface: A description of a dreadful little French child who shows their parents up.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French for 'terrible child', originally a precocious child who embarrasses adults by being candid; in English it now means a shocking, unconventional newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the borrowed French phrase names a frightful infant whose frankness mortifies adults, which is exactly the picture painted.

clue.text: Material arranged to cover a container

indicators.note: the outer word wraps round and so covers the inner pieces

parts.note: something arranged is set, as a table or a hairstyle is set
a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: Some fabric has been laid out so that it drapes over a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the synonym SET, which wraps round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin or imitation satin fabric, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Crack about the ears? It'll bring a groan

definitions.text: Crack about the ears? It'll bring a groan

parts.words: Crack about the ears? It'll bring a groan
parts.note: a crack is a joke, and one about ears of grain is one about corn; a hackneyed gag makes listeners groan

explanation.surface: A slap round the head would certainly make someone groan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack about the ears' suggests a blow to the head; read again, it is a jest whose subject is ears of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, stale gag is called corny, and such quips are traditionally greeted with groans rather than laughter.

clue.text: Freely I stream their wonderful music-making

definitions.text: Freely I stream their wonderful music-making

indicators.note: freely suggests letters let loose to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A listener lets great musicians' performances flow freely through their speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi &lit: the anagram gives the answer, and the whole clue describes the people whose music is streamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural for great conductors or virtuoso musicians, the makers of wonderful performances.

clue.text: Artwork that's not initially attractive

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: fetching means attractive or charming

explanation.surface: A piece of art that doesn't appeal at first glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' removes the F from FETCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a plate whose design has been eaten into by acid, a work of art.

clue.text: Seat in church where one keeps an animal?

definitions.meaning: an enclosed seat in a church choir or chancel
a compartment in a stable or cowshed for one animal

explanation.surface: A pew where someone apparently houses a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a choir seat in a church and the booth for a horse or cow in a barn.

clue.text: Good marks for preparing cheese

parts.note: a rating is a mark or score awarded

explanation.surface: High scores awarded to someone getting the cheese ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Grating cheese means shredding it on a rough-surfaced tool, a common step in getting it ready to cook.

clue.text: I prove agnostic about cake

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters before it are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they will show doubt over whether cake exists or matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agnostic about cake' reads like a stance on dessert, but 'about' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British sponge sandwiched with jam and cream, named after Queen Victoria.

clue.text: Lard costing nothing? Is this the healthy version?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun phrase: a fat-free product is the healthy version

parts.note: lard is pig fat
something costing nothing is free

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether free lard is the wholesome option.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that free lard is still lard, hardly healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Products stripped of fat are marketed as the slimming, wholesome alternative to the full-fat original.

clue.text: Tea, a little butter, and one piece of bread

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A snack order: a cuppa, a smear of butter and a single slice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: May she look after girl in empty nursery?

definitions.text: May she look after girl in empty nursery?

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the remaining letters
an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a carer might mind a girl in a deserted nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the wordplay builds the answer and the whole clue describes her; 'empty' leaves NY from 'nursery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is a woman employed to care for children, the very person to watch a girl in a nursery.

clue.text: Court calendar shows one hoping to be accepted

parts.note: a court hears a trial
a calendar is a list or schedule

explanation.surface: A court's schedule reveals someone trying to get admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: A triallist is a candidate taking part in a trial, such as a sports player trying out for a team selection.

clue.text: Working in parlour perhaps, go at it, not bothered

indicators.note: bothered means flustered and disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to tackle a job without fussing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags the parlour as one example; a tattoo parlour is where the inking work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattooists work in premises called parlours, where they ink designs into the skin of customers.

clue.text: Make fun of American for rejecting sweetener

indicators.note: rejecting suggests something thrown back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or make fun of them

explanation.surface: Someone teases an American who turned down the sugar in their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for rejecting' turns RAGUS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar is the standard substance used to sweeten food and drink.

clue.text: This is how senior bishop runs a TV programme

parts.note: so means in this way, like this
a pope is the most senior bishop, as the Bishop of Rome is
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A description of the way a leading cleric conducts a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'senior bishop' gives A POPE, the indefinite article included; the A after 'runs' is the clue's own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama on television about everyday lives, originally sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: Heading off north and east at first on river that runs into the Med

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the initials come after R

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Directions for heading north-east along a river flowing into the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads like setting out, but each of 'Heading off north and east' gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône flows from the Swiss Alps through France and empties into the Mediterranean near Marseille.

clue.text: Given strict instructions to be tidy

definitions.meaning: to be commanded to do something
... also means neatly arranged, in order

explanation.surface: Someone has been firmly told to keep things neat.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: commanded by an authority, and arranged neatly in an orderly way.

clue.text: Extremely happy a garden cultivated this?

definitions.text: Extremely happy a garden cultivated this?

indicators.note: extremely takes only the extremes, the first and last letters, of the next word
cultivated soil is dug and turned over, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A contented garden is assumed to have grown this flowering shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue is the definition too. HY is the outside of 'happy'; the blog folds it into the anagram, but it already stands first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are popular flowering shrubs with large mopheads of blooms, grown in many gardens.

clue.text: He was bound to prove entertaining

definitions.text: He was bound to prove entertaining

parts.words: He was bound to prove entertaining
parts.note: bound is literal: this escapologist was tied up and chained in order to entertain audiences

explanation.surface: A man who was sure to turn out to be good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as 'certain to'; it is literal, as Harry Houdini was famously tied and chained before his escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The great escapologist's act was being shackled, locked in chests or tanks, and freeing himself before amazed crowds.

clue.text: Gradually fade and have to be brought back for burial?

definitions.meaning: a sound dies away when it becomes fainter until gone

definitions.text: have to be brought back for burial?
definitions.meaning: if you ... from home your body must be brought back to be buried

explanation.surface: Someone fading slowly, then needing transport home for their funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to fade into silence, and read literally means to perish while abroad, needing repatriation.

clue.text: Fabulous Greek girl dined during festival

indicators.note: during puts one piece in the middle of the other, as an event happens within a period

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A legendary young Greek woman had dinner at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from a fable or myth: Galatea was the statue Pygmalion carved, which came to life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Galatea is the ivory statue brought to life, or a sea nymph, a figure of legend.

clue.text: One under ten confused by legal deed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A young child is bewildered by an official legal document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' acts on UNDER TEN only; the I already stands first.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal legal contract, notably one binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Only prepared new material

indicators.note: prepared means made ready by working on it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Only freshly made fabric will do.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer used as a fabric for stockings, clothing and ropes.

clue.text: Edge past farm animal, to pick this?

definitions.text: Edge past farm animal, to pick this?

indicators.note: past means beyond, so the edge goes after the animal

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
a lip is an edge, as of a cup

explanation.surface: Someone sidles round a cow to gather a wild flower.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the whole clue also hints at a field flower one might pick after skirting the livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild primula of meadows and woods, a flower one might gather.

clue.text: Some explore, leisurely, a fabulous Rhine feature

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take a relaxed look at a legendary spot on a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine, in legend home of a siren who lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Wholemeal, we note, has high temperature inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: heat is high temperature
n. is the standard abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: We point out that a brown loaf has a hot centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; 'has' is only a link word joining the two parts of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten describes bread or flour made from whole wheat grains, which is what wholemeal means.

clue.text: Is it criminal, being made to stand in line here?

definitions.text: Is it criminal, being made to stand in line here?

parts.words: Is it criminal, being made to stand in line here?
parts.note: witnesses ask whether each person in the row is the offender; suspects are made to stand in a row

explanation.surface: A complaint that being forced to queue ought to be illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a grumble about queuing; really police line up suspects so a witness can pick out the criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Police assemble a row of people including a suspect so a witness can try to pick out the offender.
